title: SDK mental models, failure modes, and 30s bootflow (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact working draft that ties together a 30-second bootflow, pragmatic mental models for new SDK adopters, explicit failure-mode mappings, and a lightweight telemetry checklist. Intention: create a single-page quick-reference that engineers and onboarding folks can use when triaging first-contact issues or iterating on quickstart docs.

Audience:
- New developer adopters (first 0–4 hours)
- Solutions / SEs running a quick demo or pilot
- DevExp writers and docs reviewers aiming for clearer flows

1) The 30-second bootflow (one-line mental model + 3 actions)
- Mental model: "I want to make a request -> see token stream -> verify telemetry"
- Action A (30s): grab API key + run a single example request (curl or one-liner)
  - Expected: 200 response, streaming body (if enabled) or generation text
  - Quick check: look for X-Request-Id in header and initial latency < 500ms for small prompt
- Action B (next 2m): switch to SDK language snippet, call simple chat/generate API, validate error handling
  - Expected: simple wrapper returns object with .id, .status, .tokens, .latency_ms
- Action C (next 5m): enable minimal telemetry and rerun, confirm telemetry appears in Console -> requests view
  - Expected telemetry: request.start, request.end, model, region, token_count, error.code (if any)

2) Mental models to surface in docs (short primer for docs copy)
- "Request vs. Stream": Explain that the same RPC can be used in sync mode (complete payload) or streaming (chunked tokens). Show both as two tiny examples.
- "Model variant hierarchy": Production model -> cheaper fallback -> quantized local model. Provide a simple ASCII tree example for rollback policies.
- "Cost versus latency knobs": map batching, kv-cache, and sequence length to cost/latency. Mention which knobs are auto-recommended by Redwood Optimize.
- "Local dev vs. Hosted difference": local stubs simulate latencies and return canned responses; hosted will include billing headers and real traces.

3) Failure modes (observable symptoms -> probable cause -> remediation)
- Symptom: immediate 401/403 from API
  - Probable cause: invalid API key, env var not set, wrong scope
  - Remediation: confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY, check team/org token scope, rotate key in secrets manager
- Symptom: high first-token latency (>2s) on small prompts
  - Probable cause: cold model load (rare for dedicated) or wrong region routing
  - Remediation: switch to pinned model region, warm model with a short dummy request, consider dedicated pool
- Symptom: partial streaming with early EOF
  - Probable cause: network proxy closing connection or client-side stream handler bug
  - Remediation: reproduce with curl --no-keepalive, inspect proxies, add reconnect/backoff in client
- Symptom: cost spikes unexpectedly
  - Probable cause: prompts with runaway loop, tokenization mismatch, forgotten default max_tokens
  - Remediation: enforce per-request token_limit, add server-side guardrails and alert on token_count anomalies
- Symptom: SDK throws deserialize error on response body
  - Probable cause: response schema changed (new fields) or streaming boundary token included
  - Remediation: use lenient parsing in client, update SDK dependency pinned version, check linked GH PRs for schema changes

4) Language quickstart snippets (kept intentionally tiny for docs)
- Curl (one-liner):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"model":"rwd-1-large","input":"Hello"}'

- Node (pseudo):
  import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'
  const client = new Redwood({ key: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
  const r = await client.generate({ model: 'rwd-1-large', input: 'Summarize: ...' })
  console.log(r.output)

- Python (pseudo):
  from redwood import Client
  c = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  resp = c.chat(model='rwd-1-large', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Hello'}])
  print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

Note: These should be trimmed to one-liners in the quickstart page; link to full examples repository for copy-paste-ready code.

5) Minimal telemetry and SLO checklist (what to surface by default)
- Per-request: request_id, model, region, latency_ms, token_count (input/output), error.code, sdk_version
- Aggregates to show in Console: p50/p95 latency, failed request rate, avg token per request, top 5 error codes, cost per 1k tokens by route
- Quick alert rules: failed request rate > 2% sustained 5m, p95 latency increase > 2x baseline, token_count spike > 3x median

6) Quick gating checklist for beginner-friendly quickstart (for docs reviewer)
- must: include working curl one-liner that returns 200 in < 1 minute (with a free-tier or demo key)
- must: show both sync and streaming example (or explicitly state streaming disabled)
- should: include one screenshot of Console showing the same request in telemetry
- should: list 3 next-steps: increase complexity, integrate SDK with retry logic, add cost guardrails
- optional: provide sandbox repo link with preseeded test key + emulation script

7) UX micro-copy suggestions (short lines for the doc)
- "Run this one line to confirm your key and region are correct."
- "Streaming gives you tokens as they arrive — use it for UI responsiveness or cancelability."
- "Set a per-request token limit to avoid surprise bills."

8) Roadmap items (small, actionable)
- Add a single-file repo that implements the 30s bootflow in 5 languages with preconfigured env and automated smoke tests (priority: JS, Python, Go)
- Add a telemetry debug page link directly in SDK error messages when present (low-cost UX win)
- Create a short "failure-mode mapper" asset for SEs to hand to customers during onboarding

9) Open questions (for next sync)
- Should quickstart one-liners include region flags by default? (impacts DX for multi-region teams)
- What SDK schema backward-compat guarantees do we make for minor releases? (affects parse guidance)
- How do we lock down an official minimal telemetry schema across self-serve and dedicated customers?

Next steps (immediate):
- Samir: prototype the tiny multi-language repo for 3 langs (due: 2024-11-22)
- Elena: draft a 1-page failure-mode cheat sheet for SEs (due: 2024-11-18)
- Ava: iterate this doc into a one-page quickstart card and attach to the docs repo PR (due: 2024-11-17)

Notes to self / scratchpad: 
- Keep examples deliberately short. People skim.
- Avoid 'magic' defaults in examples (always show token limit and model).
- Link underlying infra docs (routing, dedicated vs hosted differences) rather than repeating long explanations.
summary: Compact draft linking a 30-second bootflow to mental models, failure modes, tiny quickstart snippets, telemetry checklist, and next-step owners. Goal is a single-page asset to speed first-contact success for SDK adopters.
